subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The volume of a cube is increasing at the rate of 8 cm³/sec. How fast is the surface area increasing when the length of a side is 12 cm?

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the two formulas you would write, and say which rate you have to find on the way to the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find da/dt from the volume
steps.margin_note: First mark. "Side" here means the edge of the cube, the same a that appears in both formulas. Find da/dt before touching the surface area.
lines: Let a be the length of a side (edge) at time t. Then
(volume of a cube = a³; its surface is 6 squares,
Differentiate V = a³ with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That V = a³ is differentiated with respect to t and solved to give da/dt = 1/54 cm/sec at a = 12.
accept: differentiate v equals a cubed and find d a by d t first
eight equals four hundred thirty two times d a by d t
the edge rate links the volume rate to the area rate
modata d a by d t kanukkuni taruvatha area cheyyali
da by dt is one by fifty four centimetres per second
three into twelve squared is four hundred thirty two

steps.why: The volume rate and the surface area rate share nothing except the edge a, so da/dt has to be found before the second formula can be used.
common_mistakes: Squaring 12 as 24, which gives 72 instead of 432.
Putting a = 12 into V = a³ before differentiating, which gives dV/dt = 0.
steps.memory_tip: Two formulas, one shared letter. Whatever is given goes in the first formula, whatever is asked comes out of the second, and da/dt connects the two.

steps.label: Differentiate S = 6a² and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. dS/dt = 12a(da/dt). The 12 from the formula and the a = 12 from the question are two different 12s — write them out rather than cancelling without writing.
lines: Differentiate S = 6a² with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That S = 6a² gives dS/dt = 12a(da/dt), and substituting a = 12 with da/dt = 1/54 gives 8/3 cm²/sec.
accept: differentiate six a squared to get twelve a d a by d t
substitute a equal to twelve and d a by d t equal to one by fifty four
one hundred forty four by fifty four is eight by three
twelve a d a by d t substitute cheste eight by three vasthundi
the answer is eight by three square centimetres per second
the surface area increases at about two point six seven centimetre square per second

steps.why: 144/54 reduces by 18 to 8/3, and the reduced fraction is the expected final form. The unit cm²/sec follows from an area changing per second.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as 144/54 without reducing it.
Writing the unit as cm³/sec instead of cm²/sec.
steps.memory_tip: A cube has six equal square faces, so S = 6a², and its derivative doubles the 6 into 12a.

insider_note: Two steps: find da/dt from dV/dt = 3a²(da/dt), then feed it into dS/dt = 12a(da/dt). Finding da/dt first is the simplest method.
